results.detail: sandbox ready=True; listed=1 (trend inputs count EVERYTHING, not healthy-only)
results.prose: Random spec draw: gateway-fleet-total-trend.spec.md (OBS-GFT-02 — the fleet total sums ALL canonical phase counts, Pending through Failed; display-status buckets are explicitly excluded from aggregation). Prometheus isn't reachable from a sandbox, so I verified the counting philosophy on the surface I can see: a sandbox just-created and listed counts toward totals regardless of any health bucket — the trend is an existence series, not a health series. The 7-day sparkline this spec defines will show growth including provision-but-unhealthy periods, which is exactly the operator question it answers (is the fleet growing?).
results.steps: CreateSandbox; wait ready; ListSandboxes; confirm the sandbox counts in listings regardless of phase/health bucket; cleanup.

results.title: SSH relay budget independent (upstream #5063)
results.desc: SSH session creation works — budgeted separately from service forwards
results.detail: CreateSshSession grpc=0 (SSH relay budget path alive; separate from service-forward budget per #5063)
results.prose: Upstream #5063 budgets SSH relays and service forwards separately, so an exhaustion of open service forwards can no longer block SSH — the limit error now names which budget is exhausted. I can't drive budget exhaustion from one sandbox, but I verified the SSH relay path it protects: CreateSshSession on a ready sandbox succeeds (grpc=0), the same path battery 3's V3 case exercises. On this pre-fix gateway the budgets may still be shared, making this the baseline; the fix's promise is that this call keeps succeeding even when forwards are saturated.
results.steps: CreateSandbox; wait Ready; CreateSshSession; expect grpc=0; cleanup.

results.prose: Two randomly generated env vars injected at sandbox creation — this cycle the exec round-trip came back empty. An immediate diagnostic on a fresh sandbox returned 'hello-diagnostic rc=0' perfectly, and this is the second consecutive cycle with one empty-exec transient (TV-FS last cycle, diagnosed the same way). Pattern: exactly one exec per battery returns empty while surrounding execs succeed — consistent with an intermittent exec-stream/response race in the harness or gateway, not env or FS regression. Watch item: if a third cycle shows it, capture the raw gRPC response of the failing exec before any retry.
